courses.subject: BUS
courses.title: Legal Environment of Business
courses.description: Fundamental legal principles pertaining to business transactions. Introduction to the law as an instrument of social and political control in society. Topics include sources of law and ethics, contracts, torts, agency, judicial and administrative processes, employment law, forms of business organizations, and domestic and international governmental regulations. (Same as Same as LAW 105). CSU/UC

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Law and Society
courses.description: Overview of the legal system including the courts, participants and various sources of law in the American legal system. Review of the legal and judicial process in the United States covering the adversarial system, jurisdiction of federal and state courts, and the general process of judicial review. Explanation of different sources of law including statutes, court cases and administrative agency rules. Review of basic legal reasoning and introductory legal research methods. Examination of legal ethics. Introduction to substantive areas of law and the effect the law has in various groups and individuals in our system. Same as PARA 100. (Same as Same as: PARA 100). CSU/UC

courses.title: Legal Environment of Business
courses.description: Fundamental legal principles pertaining to business transactions. Introduction to the law as an instrument of social and political control in society. The course will explore the application of the California Rules of Professional Conduct as applied to the legal profession and society in general. (Same as Paralegal 121). CSU/UC

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legal Interpretation and Translation Spanish / English
courses.description: Legal Spanish and English bilingual skills required for interpreters and translators to provide professional interpreting and translating services to law offices, courts, law enforcement, government, and other legal related business. Topics include proper translation of legal terminology, consecutive mode of interpreting in a legal setting, professional role, standards, code of ethics, documents, forms, court reporting, and legal cases. Students must be fluent in both Spanish and English (oral and written) to be confirmed by instructor with first assignment. (Same as Business Application 133). CSU

courses.title: Mock Trial
courses.description: This course introduces students to the structure and practice of the American legal system through the simulation of a courtroom trial. Students will actively participate as attorneys, witnesses, and jurors in mock trials to gain hands-on experience in trial procedures, legal research, case preparation, courtroom etiquette, and argumentation. The course emphasizes critical thinking, courtroom presentation, while offering insight into legal careers such as litigation, criminal law, and legal advocacy. Field trip may be required. CSU

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Law and Society
courses.description: Overview of the legal system including the courts, participants and various sources of law in the American legal system and how society is affected. Review of the legal and judicial process in the United States covering the adversarial system, jurisdiction of federal and state courts, and the general process of judicial review and how different segments of society are affected. Explanation of different sources of law including statutes, court cases and administrative agency rules. Review of basic legal reasoning and introductory legal research methods. Introduction to substantive areas of law and the effect the law has in various groups and individuals in our system. Review of the role and regulation of legal professionals, legal ethics and consumer protection laws, and their effect on providing legal services to various segments of society. (Same as Law 100). CSU/UC

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Law Office Management
courses.description: Structure and procedures of the law office. Emphasis on time management, the role of paralegals and paralegal administrators in the law office, ethics in the law office, client property regulations, time keeping and billing, and technology management in a law office. CSU

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Principles and Procedures in the Criminal Justice System
courses.description: An examination and analysis of due process in criminal proceedings from pre-arrest through trial and appeal, utilizing statutory law and state and constitutional law precedents. (Same as Criminal Justice 107). (Same as Paralegal 107). CSU

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Global Commerce and Management
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of global commerce, focusing on the creation and management of international business contracts, financial mechanisms, and the regulatory frameworks that govern international distribution. Students will learn about international limited liability companies, foreign direct investment, and how global trade agreements such as NAFTA/USMCA, GATT, and the EU affect businesses. The course also explores management in varying legal environments and U.S. export regulations. Emphasis will be placed on using the U.N. Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods and managing cross-border transactions. Through this course, students will gain insight into how countries cooperate to form global markets and regulate international trade. (Same as BUS 117). CSU

courses.description: Study of basic substantive law and procedures in family law. Court procedures for divorce, annulment, temporary and permanent support, restraining orders, division of community property, and child custody procedures including adoption and paternity actions. CSU

courses.title: Law of Business Organizations
courses.description: Laws of the California Corporations Code. Students prepare articles of incorporation, minutes, by-laws, stock, and stock transfer. Agency law and partnership laws. Students will understand compliance regulations. CSU

courses.description: Basic study of Immigration Law in the United States, with focus on preparation of those forms used by immigrants to secure benefits. Marketing procedures for paralegals involved in Immigration Law will be analyzed, and ethical considerations to avoid the illegal practice of law will be covered. CSU

courses.title: Formerly: Discovery Techniques
courses.description: Focus on the discovery phase of litigation with specific instruction on eDiscovery. Practical applications for paralegals. CSU

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Civil Litigation Overview
courses.description: Overview of California procedures from acceptance of a case through trial. Planning litigation, motions, discovery, and trial preparation. Preparation of pleadings. Overview of California discovery rules, preparation of discovery documents, and responses. CSU

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Tort Law and Alternative Dispute Resolution
courses.description: Learn about the different types of Torts including: intentional torts, negligence, strict liability, product liability, damages, immunity, and defenses to torts. Learn how to apply principles of insurance law and procedures for the investigation of personal injury cases. Students will review the principles of dispute resolution through negotiation, mediation, and arbitration. Students will mediate impartially and use tools to maximize negotiation effectiveness. The course includes application of mediation skills in the law office. CSU

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Legal Transactions
courses.description: Introduction to contracts and drafting legal documents for corporations and real estate transactions. Topics include: contract formation, performance, breach, and third party interests. Students will learn the laws of the California Corporations Code and the laws governing real estate transactions. Learn how to draft various contracts and other documents and select, edit, and customize formbook and computerized forms in real property, corporations, family law, and estate planning. CSU

courses.subject: PARA

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: Advanced Research and Writing
courses.description: Advanced projects in legal research and writing with an emphasis on legal structure and style. Students must pass Para 246 with a C or better prior to taking Para 248. CSU

courses.subject: PARA
courses.title: The Professional Paralegal
courses.description: This is the capstone class to the Paralegal associate degree and certificate. Students will demonstrate their knowledge of ethics, legal principles, and the technical skills necessary for entry level employment as a paralegal. This course is to be taken in the semester of or prior to graduation. This course will include preparation of graduation petitions, professional resumes and a professional portfolio that will include work prepared in PARA 101, PARA 121, PARA 120, PARA 145 and PARA 150. Students will be required to certify they are in the second to last or last semester prior to graduation. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. CSU

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
